title: Camlin Fine Sciences Ltd - 532834 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Camlin Q4 FY26 revenue about INR424 crores and EBITDA INR21 crores (5% margin), hit by a roughly 20% quarterly sales shortfall from shipping and war-related disruption.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was weak: management said sales were hit by about 20% from shipment delays, freight shortages and longer transit times linked to the Middle East conflict. Revenue was about INR424 crores in the quarter, with total revenue of INR1,723 crores after moving discontinued operations out. EBITDA was INR21 crores (5%), with vanillin sales largely from channel stock and Blends growth of 17%, short of the 20% target. Management said FY27 guidance is unchanged: revenue INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin 12-14%. The CFS Europe liquidation produced a gain of about INR100 crores and removes ongoing cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year.

financial_highlights.change: about INR53 crores lower after discontinued-business reclassification

financial_highlights.metric: Gain from discontinued operations (CFS Europe derecognition)
financial_highlights.value: about INR85 crores in PBT, about INR100 crores gain on loss of control as stated

financial_highlights.change: 18% including discontinued Blends business in Europe; target was about 20%

financial_highlights.value: about INR670 crores, including INR30 crores in escrow for Vinpai open offer
financial_highlights.change: up about INR50 crores YoY; Italian loans of about INR85 crores knocked out

segments.name: Straights (TBHQ, BHA and others)
segments.commentary: Management said market share was held, but revenue fell on local competition and pricing pressure. Some Straights volume is being shifted into Blends. TBHQ prices have corrected upward and BHA is slightly above pre-war levels.

segments.name: Blends (incl. Vinpai and Vitafor)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth was 17% against a 20% target. Vinpai ran at about INR17 crores over three months against an expected INR10 crores a month. Management guides Blends to upwards of INR1,400 crores in FY27, with Vinpai and Vitafor each at roughly 14-16 million (USD) and above EBITDA breakeven in FY27.

segments.name: Vanillin (methyl and ethyl)
segments.commentary: Methyl production stopped from 15 January for conversion to ethyl vanillin; Q4 sales came mainly from internal US channel stock. Ethyl orders of about 300 tonnes are on hand for Q1, with a 600-tonne ethyl campaign planned. FY27 US volume is guided at 2,200-2,400 tonnes, and Europe at 1,500-1,600 tonnes.

segments.name: Diphenol (hydroquinone and catechol)
segments.commentary: Diphenol production was discontinued on 22 May. Phenol rose from about INR85 to above INR150/kg, and about 3,000 tonnes of catechol stock covers 8-9 months of vanillin output. Hydroquinone will be imported from China.

segments.name: CFS Europe and China
segments.commentary: CFS Europe was liquidated, and its cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year ends from next quarter. China is still in liquidation, with costs expected at INR7-8 crores next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin at 12-14%; management said guidance is not changing.
FY27 blended vanillin realisation expected at about $13.5-14/kg after tariffs, with US tariff at 15.5% (5.5% base plus 10%).
Q1 FY27 vanillin realisation expected to rise over Q4; gross margin guided to hold at about 48%, give or take 1%.
Q1 FY27 combined US and Europe vanillin sales expected to grow over Q4 FY26; Q1 EBITDA said to be hard to call, with the full diphenol-discontinuation impact in Q2.
Vinpai and Vitafor expected above EBITDA breakeven in FY27; Blends guided to upwards of INR1,400 crores.
Management said a stable 10-15% growth over the next two quarters would be great, citing elevated freight and feedstock costs.
Anticipated US tariff refund of about INR9-10 crores (about 50% cash, 50% duty adjustment, per management) on duties paid until February.
Repayment of about INR60-70 crores in FY27; equity raise described as a last resort, with structured or bank debt being pursued.
capex_capacity: A fire on Saturday (about 23 May) at the Dahej plant was contained, with no spread to the whole plant; insurance cover is adequate, but there will be some loss.
Diphenol plant shut on 22 May; management is evaluating repurposing it into a multipurpose facility to cut raw material costs.
Methyl-to-ethyl vanillin conversion took about 2 months, and ethyl vanillin production has started. Methyl production resumed in April.
FY27 vanillin volume at 70% utilisation implies about 4,000-4,200 tonnes, with the gap of about 1,000 tonnes to be sourced as catechol or guaiacol from China.
Management said the company has increased its authorised capital in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Vanillin: Syensqo is pricing DDP US at about $17-18/kg; Camlin's net realisation is about $13 after holding, tariff and financing costs. Management expects Syensqo to raise prices to $19-20 once its capacity reaches 100%.

Raw materials: phenol rose from about INR85 to above INR150/kg. Total raw material cost was about $7.5/kg before the war and is now about $9/kg; caustic has about doubled and freight to the Americas is about three times the pre-war cost.
Logistics: shipments that were expected in 20 days now take 40-50 days, and management expects it to take about a quarter for normalisation.
Management said demand for 4,000 tonnes of vanillin is achievable; the bigger constraints are working capital, logistics and cash flow.
Management did not expect the EBITDA impact of the conflict to be resolved quickly; it estimated sales were hit by about INR50 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vanillin volumes reach only about 320 tonnes in Q4 when about 650 tonnes was held in the channel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100 tonnes was sold in Q3 and the plan was to hold back a further 200 tonnes. About 300 tonnes of channel stock remains for Q1, so the total is about 600 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA shortfall was due to the Middle East crisis, and is guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales were hit by about INR50 crores and Vinpai had about INR10 crores of EBITDA loss from liquidity issues, so EBITDA would have been about INR30 crores higher. FY27 guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended vanillin realisation for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be about $13.5-14/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt ended FY26 at about INR670 crores, including INR30 crores in escrow, with repayments of INR60-70 crores in FY27. Management prefers structured or bank debt, and equity is a last resort.

qa_highlights.question: Is the vanillin cost base higher now, and can the company reach INR300-330 crores of EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the vanillin cost is about $10.5/kg against $13.5 realisation, which implies about INR22-23 crores on 800 tonnes in Q1. Group EBITDA guidance is 12-14% on INR2,200-2,400 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US tariff refund cash or duty adjustment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is typically about 50% cash and 50% adjusted against duty, with about INR9-10 crores on a few months of India vanillin turnover.

risks_watch: Working capital and cash flow: long shipping cycles, debt of about INR670 crores and INR60-70 crores of repayments in FY27.
Raw material and freight inflation: phenol above INR150/kg, caustic about doubled, freight costs elevated and supply intermittent.
Q1 EBITDA visibility is low because of the diphenol shutdown and Chinese hydroquinone sourcing.
Dahej plant fire: the loss amount and insurance settlement are not yet quantified.
Whether the US tariff refund arrives in cash or as duty adjustment, and the timing.
Whether Syensqo raises prices as expected, and the ethyl/methyl campaign timing.
Pace of Vinpai and Vitafor ramp-up, and whether Blends reaches INR1,400 crores in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on strategy and long-term Blends and vanillin demand, but cautious on near-term margins and logistics. Management was frank that Q4 was disrupted and that Q1 and Q2 remain uncertain. Several answers were evasive on the cost of structured debt and on the Q1 EBITDA outlook.
key_quotes: This quarter, the sale was impacted by around 20% due to delay in shipments, lack of ships and increased freight time to our markets across the globe.
One good thing about this is the cash burn on this discontinued operations of around INR50 crores, INR60 crores every year is going to come to zero from next quarter, and that's a big cost saving.
Capital infusion is the last resort. We are in the market for debt at this moment.
So what we had said the 1,500, 1,600 ton for the year, I think we are good for that.

adds.what: Ethyl vanillin conversion from methyl (existing US vanillin plant, conversion took ~2 months; ethyl production started)
Diphenol plant shut 22 May; management evaluating repurposing into multipurpose facility (capacity reduction, not addition)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided INR2,200-2,400 crores (about 30-40% over the implied FY26 base, but the brief gives no FY26 base, so the growth % is not computed) and EBITDA margin 12-14%, held; backing is partial: ~300 t ethyl orders on hand for Q1 and a 600 t campaign, Blends >INR1,400 crores, but no firm contracts for the full year, and Q4 revenue fell ~20% short on shipping disruption.
